_comment: DECLARED EXECUTABLE DEPENDENCIES — port Phase 0, Gate A deliverable #2:
'reproduce all executable dependencies in a clean CI environment'.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (ROADMAP 9h): package.json declares acorn, jsdom and ws, but
tools/uilayout.js and tools/bootperf.js drive a REAL browser — they spawn a system
binary over CDP. There is no Playwright, no Puppeteer, no npm driver anywhere in
tools/. So `npm install` on a clean clone silently leaves TWO of the nine suites
unrunnable, and nothing said so until 2026-07-31.
Verified by `node tools/preflight.js`. This file is the single source for the pin;
preflight reads it rather than hard-coding anything.

node._comment: Matches jsdom's supported Node lines; verifiedWith is what Gate A evidence was actually produced on.

packages._comment: From package.json. `npm install` provisions these; preflight only confirms they resolve.

_comment: NOT an npm package. A system binary, spawned headless and driven over CDP.
⚠ Addendum D: a layout gate whose thresholds were set on one browser revision
drifts on the next. uilayout.js compares against STORED numbers (787 checks /
10 viewports), so that result is only meaningful against a known revision.
TREAT A VERSION BUMP AS AN EXPLICIT RE-BASELINE, NOT A REGRESSION.

pinned.name: Microsoft Edge
pinned._comment: Edge auto-updates silently on Windows. Expect drift; preflight WARNS rather than fails, because a bump is a decision, not a defect.

browser._resolutionNote: This declared order mirrors port/v2/tools/browserpath.mjs. Preflight, uilayout and bootperf all invoke that one negative-controlled resolver; uilayout also consumes the shared browsercdp lifecycle, while bootperf lifecycle migration remains open.

gatesRequiringBrowser.uilayout: PASS, 787 checks / 10 viewports (on the pinned revision)
gatesRequiringBrowser.bootperf: not re-run for v1.8.9; the v1.8.5 PASS stands
